neighbours.label: the point where a sentence continues into a claim that something will not or cannot happen ('and it never will', 'and is unlikely to')
fire: Nobody has ever climbed that wall, and nobody ever will.
A cure for the common cold doesn't exist yet and is unlikely to appear soon.
The old mill has not reopened, and it never will.
Peace talks have failed before and cannot succeed without both sides.
My brother has never apologised and probably never will.
Such a machine has not been built and may never be built.
The team hasn't won a title in decades and is unlikely to win one now.
That promise was never kept, and it never could be.
quiet: Many people have climbed that wall, and more will try next summer.
A new vaccine is being tested and is due to appear next spring.
The old mill has been restored and reopens in May.
Peace talks are scheduled to resume next week in Geneva.
My brother apologised yesterday and brought flowers.
Such a machine was built last year and runs every day.
The team won a title last season and hopes to repeat it.
That promise was kept, and the bridge opened on time.

notes: Card: peaks on ' never' in 'it never will', ' and' before 'is unlikely', '(and cannot have)'; output suppresses future/upcoming/planned, and the - pole is scheduled/promised/slated, the other side (planned futures). Probe: 0.21-0.25 on such continuations, ~0 on 'scheduled'.
